name: Chalkboard
summary: A clean classroom blackboard on which chalk writes itself in true stroke order, no hand or eraser in sight: deep green slate, grainy white chalk, one accent chalk for the one thing the lesson tracks, a pale second hand for what people think, wiped in one damp pass and rewritten in the same place.

palette.use: the darker back panel and the slate's shadowed edges
white chalk: all structure (words, lines, labels, arrows)
the accent chalk for the one component the lesson tracks; this film tracks blue light, so it is a pale blue (proposed)
the source's accent chalk (orange), for a tracked component with no colour of its own
second-hand chalk (pale yellow): another person's handwriting, what people think
painted rule lines on the slate, at 24–36%
the warm white wall in wide shots
the green dado below the wall
the damp cloth's wet streak, at 36%, drying back

display.note: board writing is drawn by the style's own single-stroke chalk hand, not a font; Alegreya italic is the subtitle plate's face

type.emphasis: the accent chalk on the one tracked component, an underline, or a circle

banned: a dirty board: old swirls, ghost lessons, floating dust or bokeh
a hand, a chalk stick or an eraser on screen while writing
anything typeset or faded in on the board (it isn't a slide): things are written, wiped, slid in or dry
the accent chalk on arrows or decoration that isn't the tracked component
rainbow or gradient chalk, or more than three chalks
a perspective tilt: the camera faces the board flat on
a glossy white board, markers or magnets (that's Whiteboard)
